articles.title: Lovable vs Bolt.new (2026): which AI app builder should you use?
articles.desc: Lovable vs Bolt.new compared for people who don't code: free plans, the $25 paid plans, hosting and domains, and which one we'd pick. Prices checked 10 Nov 2026.
articles.verdict: Pick Lovable if you don't code and want the shortest route from a description to a working full-stack web app. It's our No. 1 app builder. Pick Bolt.new if you want to tinker in the browser on a bigger free allowance, with hosting included even on the free plan. Both start at $25/month when you go paid.
articles.body:
The main differences

  • How usage is counted. Lovable uses credits: a small change like "make the button gray" costs about 0.5 credits, and a landing page with generated images about 1.7, according to its pricing page. Bolt.new counts tokens: 1M a month on the free plan (300K a day), and Pro starts at 10M a month with no daily limit.
  • Hosting and domains. Bolt.new includes website hosting and unlimited databases on every plan. Custom domains and removing the Bolt branding need Pro. Lovable says hosting a small or new app is usually covered by the Cloud credits included with every plan.
  • Teams. Lovable charges per workspace, not per seat, so you can invite as many people as you like to share the credits. Bolt.new Teams is $30 per member a month.

Not sure you need an app builder at all? See the best AI coding tools for non-developers or the full app builder ranking.

who.Lovable: Non-coders who want a full-stack web app (pages, logins, data) built by chatting, and teams who want to share one pot of credits.
who.Bolt.new: People who want to experiment for free in the browser, and who want hosting, databases and their own domain in one $25 plan.

faq: Is Lovable or Bolt.new cheaper?
They cost the same to start: Lovable Pro is $25/month for 100 credits ($21/month billed annually) and Bolt.new Pro is $25/month, with up to 28% off billed yearly. Checked 10 Nov 2026.
Which free plan is better?
They measure usage differently. Lovable's free plan gives 5 build credits a day (up to 30 a month). Bolt.new's gives 1M tokens a month, up to 300K a day, and puts Bolt branding on your site.
Can I use my own domain?
On Bolt.new, custom domains are part of Pro ($25/month). We haven't confirmed Lovable's custom domain terms on its own pages this time, so check its pricing page before you buy.
Do I own what I build?
Lovable's pricing FAQ says you own the code and the apps you build. We haven't verified Bolt.new's terms on this point.

articles.desc: Lovable vs Replit Agent compared: free plans, paid plans ($25 vs $20/month), publishing apps and who each suits. Prices checked 10 Nov 2026.
articles.verdict: Pick Lovable for the quickest path from an idea to a polished web app. Pick Replit if you want building, databases and publishing in one place, and want the cheaper paid plan (Core is $20/month against Lovable's $25). who.Lovable: Non-coders who want the fastest route to a finished-looking web app.
who.Replit: People who want build, database and hosting in one product, and may grow into its more powerful paid Agent modes.

faq: Is Replit free?
Yes, the Starter plan is free with no time limit. It includes a daily Agent allowance, monthly cloud credits and one published app that goes down after 30 days (Replit docs, checked 10 Nov 2026).
Which is cheaper, Lovable or Replit?

articles.title: Cursor vs GitHub Copilot (2026): which AI coding assistant is worth paying for?
articles.desc: Cursor vs GitHub Copilot: free plans, Copilot Pro at $10 vs Cursor Plus at $8 and Premium at $30, which editors they work in, and our pick. Checked 10 Nov 2026.
articles.verdict: Pick GitHub Copilot if you want to stay in the editor you already use: it works in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode, Neovim, Eclipse and Zed, and Pro is $10/month with unlimited completions. Pick Cursor if you want an AI-first editor and the strongest agent features. Cloud agents and other companies' models start on Premium at $30/month.
articles.body:
The main differences

  • Where it runs. Cursor is its own editor. Copilot plugs into the editor you already use, the terminal (Copilot CLI) and GitHub itself.
  • The cheap plans. Cursor Plus is $8/month, but it only includes Grok models. Copilot Pro is $10/month with unlimited inline suggestions and $15 a month of AI credits for chat and agents.
  • The serious plans. Cursor Premium ($30/month) adds cloud agents and automations, AI code reviews, and other companies' models billed at API list price. Copilot Pro+ ($39/month) adds premium models and more included usage.
  • How you buy it. Cursor plans are sold through X Subscription Corp and bundle X and Grok features. Copilot is billed by GitHub.

Want the three-way version with Windsurf? See Cursor vs Windsurf vs GitHub Copilot and the AI code editor ranking.

who.Cursor: People who code most days and want one AI-native editor with agents, cloud agents and automations.
who.GitHub Copilot: Anyone happy in VS Code, JetBrains, Xcode and the rest who wants dependable AI help at the lowest solid price.

faq: Is GitHub Copilot free?
Yes. Copilot Free includes 2,000 inline suggestions a month and limited chat and agent use, with no credit card (checked 10 Nov 2026).
Is Cursor free?
Yes. Cursor's free plan includes limited agent and chat requests.
Which is cheaper?
Cursor Plus is $8/month but only includes Grok models. Copilot Pro is $10/month. Cursor Premium, which adds cloud agents and other companies' models at API list price, is $30/month.
Can I use Claude or GPT models?

On Copilot Pro, the pricing page lists models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI, with some reserved for Pro+. On Cursor, other companies' models need Premium or higher and are billed at API list price.

articles.title: Builder.io vs Figma Make (2026): which turns your designs into code?
articles.desc: Builder.io vs Figma Make for design-to-code: free plans, Builder.io Pro at $24 vs a $16 Figma Full seat, prototype vs production code. Checked 10 Nov 2026.
articles.verdict: Pick Figma Make if you want a working prototype from your designs without leaving Figma. It's our No. 1 design-to-code tool, and a Professional Full seat is $16/month. Pick Builder.io if the code has to land in a real codebase and use your own components. It connects to GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket and has a free plan. Builder.io is a ShipRank affiliate, which doesn't change its No. 2 spot.
articles.body:
The main differences

  • What comes out. Figma Make turns prompts and designs into functional prototypes and web apps inside Figma. Builder.io connects to your Git repo and design system, with a Figma plugin and a VS Code extension, so changes go into your codebase.
  • Free plans. Figma's Starter plan includes Make with up to 150 AI credits a day (500 a month), but no team libraries. Builder.io Free gives 15 credits a day (60 a month) and one design system.
  • Paid plans. A Figma Professional Full seat is $16/month with 3,000 AI credits. Dev seats only let you try Make in drafts. Builder.io Pro is $24/user/month with 500 credits and up to 3 design systems. Extra credits are $25 per 500.

For the full walkthrough, read how to turn Figma designs into code with AI or see the design-to-code ranking.

who.Figma Make: Designers and founders who want something clickable to test or show people, fast.
who.Builder.io: Teams with an existing codebase and component library who want designs turned into code their developers will merge.

faq: Is Figma Make free?

Yes, with limits. It's on Figma's free Starter plan, which has 150 AI credits a day and up to 500 a month. Starter users must also publish to the Figma Community to publish to the public web (Figma Help Center, checked 10 Nov 2026).
Is Builder.io free?
Yes. Builder.io's free plan gives 15 credits a day (60 a month max) and includes Git connections, the Figma plugin and the VS Code extension.
Does ShipRank earn money from Builder.io?
Yes. Builder.io links on this page are affiliate links, so we may earn a commission if you buy. That doesn't change our ranking, which still puts Figma Make first.
